Second release of the **Docker packaging + graphical web interface** for
Polymer. This repository is a fork of [hygeos/polymer](https://github.com/hygeos/polymer);
the Polymer algorithm itself is unchanged. Docker packaging and interface by
**Francesco Tarini** ([@frabolla](https://github.com/frabolla)).

> Polymer is free for non-commercial use and **must not be redistributed**
> (see `LICENCE.TXT`), so no image is published here — you build it locally and
> accept the terms on first run.

## Upgrading from v0.1.0

Download the new version, then double-click the launcher: it rebuilds the image.
Your `data/` folder (credentials, auxiliary data, results) is kept as it is.

## What's new

**Processing**
- **PRISMA on real data**: checks that both the L1 and its L2C companion are
  present, and explains clearly what is missing.
- **Copernicus ERA5 / CDS** as the meteorological source, alongside NASA
  Earthdata. The source is now an explicit choice for each run; nothing is
  assumed.
- **Land handling**: mask land (default), **correct land pixels too**, or use
  the Global Surface Water mask.
- Clearer error messages. For example, choosing a meteo source whose account is
  not saved is caught before the run starts.

**Interface**
- A focused one-time setup page on first launch; after that, tabs with
  Processing first.
- The auxiliary data download runs in the background and can be cancelled.
  It recovers automatically after an interrupted download.
- **Working folders** panel: see where input/output are on your computer, and
  move them (e.g. to an external drive).
- While a job runs, the other tabs stay usable.

**Reliability and security** (full review)
- NASA passwords with spaces or `#` now work.
- Zips made with macOS Finder (**Compress**) extract correctly.
- The "change folders" option refuses whole disks and system folders.
- The output file name can no longer point outside the output folder.
- The Copernicus key is no longer shown in the page.
- Credential files are private from the moment they are created.
- On Linux the app runs as your user, so the files in `data/` stay yours.
- Windows: fixes for DNS failures during downloads and for slow base-image
  downloads during the build.
- CI now builds and smoke-tests the image on native amd64 and arm64 on every
  change. It had never completed before this release.

## Getting started

1. Install Docker Desktop.
2. Download this repository (**Code → Download ZIP**) and unzip it.
3. Double-click `docker/launchers/Start-Polymer-macOS-Linux.command` or
   `Start-Polymer-Windows.bat`. The first build takes 10–20 min.
4. The browser opens at `http://localhost:8501`.

Step-by-step guides: [`docker/HOWTO.md`](docker/HOWTO.md) /
[`docker/HOWTO.it.md`](docker/HOWTO.it.md) (also attached below).
